Solution 1 is wrong. Fejér–Riesz applied to $M^2-|P|^2$ gives $M^2 \ge 6$, so $\sqrt{5}$ is impossible.

Solutions 2 and 3 are also wrong. Both claim $M \approx 2.661$, but that value is not minimal. Take $a=d=1$ and $b=c=e^{i\beta}$ with $\cos\beta = -0.23$, so $P(z)=z^3+bz^2+bz+1$. At $z=1$, $|P(1)|^2 = 4|1+b|^2 = 8+8\cos\beta \approx 6.16$, so $M \approx 2.48$. On the circle, $|P|^2 = 4+2g(x)$ with $x=\cos\theta$, and $g(x)=4x^3-0.92x^2-2.46x+0.46$ has interior maximum about $1.04$, below the endpoint value $g(1)=1.08$. So the maximum of $|P|^2$ is about $6.16$, which is below $6.83$ (the value $4+16\sqrt{3}/9 \approx 7.08$ from Solutions 2 and 3 is itself larger still).

So no solution gives the minimum. I have not determined the true minimal $M$.

CHOICE: NONE
CONFIDENCE: 4
